title: Clinical Perimetry: Kinetic vs. Static Strategies
summary: Mastering the physics and clinical applications of visual field testing is essential for detecting glaucomatous progression and neuro-ophthalmological defects. This guide contrasts traditional kinetic perimetry with modern automated static threshold techniques.

sections.title: Definition & Foundations
sections.content: Perimetry measures the differential light sensitivity across the visual field. Kinetic perimetry (Goldmann) involves moving a stimulus of constant intensity toward the fixation point until detection (isopters). Static perimetry measures the threshold sensitivity at fixed locations by varying stimulus intensity (decibels, dB).

sections.title: Clinical Indications
content: Kinetic: Detecting peripheral contractions (e.g., Retinitis Pigmentosa, advanced Glaucoma).
Static: Early detection of glaucomatous damage (RNFL thinning).
Static: Longitudinal monitoring of VF index progression.

sections.title: Red Flags in Testing
content: False Positives (>15%): Suggests 'trigger-happy' patient; elevates sensitivity.
False Negatives (>20%): Suggests inattention or advanced field loss.
Gaze Tracking Errors: Significant misalignment during testing.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Patient education and lens correction (near addition calculated per age).
Step 2: Trial frame alignment (check for rim artifacts).
Step 3: Fixation monitoring (Heijl-Krakau method for blind spot).
Step 4: Threshold strategy selection (SITA Fast vs. SITA Standard).
Step 5: Analysis of Global Indices (Mean Deviation, Pattern SD).

content.explanation: Fixation losses (check blind spot), False-positives (trigger-happy), False-negatives (inattention).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always adjust for age: Thresholds naturally decline with aging due to miosis and media opacities.
The 'Hill of Vision': Imagine the central fovea as the peak; sensitivity drops rapidly toward the periphery.
SITA (Swedish Interactive Threshold Algorithm) reduces test time by 50% compared to traditional Full Threshold.
Look for 'biconcave' patterns in bitemporal hemianopia (chiasmal pathology).
Artifacts: Eyelid ptosis or trial lens rims can create 'pseudoscotomas' in superior fields.
